original_question: For each constant delta > 0, do s^{-O(1)}-biased densities delta-fool all size-s DNF formulas; equivalently, if f : {0,1}^n -> {-1,1} is computable by a size-s DNF and phi is an s^{-O(1)}-biased density on {0,1}^n, must |E_{x~{0,1}^n}[f(x)] - E_{y~phi}[f(y)]| <= delta?
target_in_paper: The survey open problem titled "ε-biased Sets for DNFs" in arXiv:1204.6447 (main matter, pp. 9-10), sourced there to [DETT10].
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper extremely closely: it preserves the leading quantifier "for each constant δ > 0," the target class "size-s DNF formulas," the desired bias scale "s^{-O(1)}," and the paper’s expectation-based unpacking of what it means to δ-fool a DNF. It also matches the survey’s {-1,1}-valued formulation of the test function.
missing_details: The phrase "s^{-O(1)}-biased" hides a quantifier that should be made explicit: for each fixed constant δ > 0, the question is whether there exists a constant c = c(δ) > 0 such that bias at most s^{-c} suffices.
A stand-alone version should define what "ε-biased" means: for every nonempty S ⊆ [n], the distribution φ must satisfy |E_{y∼φ}[χ_S(y)]| ≤ ε, where χ_S(x) = ∏_{i∈S} (-1)^{x_i}.
The ambient reference distribution should be named explicitly as the uniform distribution U_n on {0,1}^n.
The object called a "density" in the survey should be stated explicitly as a probability distribution on {0,1}^n.
The meaning of "size-s DNF" should be made explicit: a DNF formula on n Boolean variables with at most s terms, each term being an AND of literals.
The universal scope over parameters should be stated explicitly: for all n and all size parameters s (not just for one fixed n or one fixed DNF).

To avoid mixing encodings, a stand-alone statement should either stay consistently with {-1,1}-valued functions or else consistently use {0,1}-valued DNFs; the paper’s survey statement uses the {-1,1} encoding.
refined_question: For every fixed constant δ > 0, does there exist a constant c = c(δ) > 0 such that, for all n and s ≥ 1, every probability distribution φ on {0,1}^n satisfying |E_{y∼φ}[χ_S(y)]| ≤ s^{-c} for every nonempty S ⊆ [n] δ-fools every DNF formula on n variables with at most s terms? Equivalently, if f : {0,1}^n → {-1,1} is computable by a DNF of size at most s and φ is s^{-c}-biased in the above sense, must |E_{x∼U_n}[f(x)] - E_{y∼φ}[f(y)]| ≤ δ?
justification: In arXiv:1204.6447 itself, the exact target is the survey item "ε-biased Sets for DNFs," and your draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of that item. The survey’s statement is brief, so I made explicit the hidden quantifier inside s^{-O(1)}, the meaning of ε-bias via nontrivial parity characters, the role of the uniform distribution U_n, and the standard term-count meaning of DNF size. I did not broaden the scope to width-w DNFs, read-once DNFs, or AC0. The nearby context in the survey and in DETT10 shows why this exact sharpening is the paper-faithful one: DETT10 proves general-DNF fooling only for much smaller bias, namely roughly exp(-O(log^2(s/δ) log log(s/δ))), proves a stronger polynomial-bias result only for read-once DNFs, and gives lower bounds showing that for general DNFs one needs bias at least m^{-Ω(log(1/δ))} in the low-error regime. So the open problem is specifically whether polynomially small bias in s suffices once δ is fixed as a constant.
